mappings.note: Definition recall: names the middle observation of ordered data as the median. Mean and mode are distractors only, so LO-3 and not LO-1/LO-2.
Proves the deviation property Sum f(x - xbar) = 0, which is the algebra of the direct-method mean formula. No median or mode is touched.

Empirical relation Mode = 3 Median - 2 Mean, used to recover the mean from the other two. No LO covers the empirical relation (see defect note); LO-1 is wrong because no direct/assumed/step-deviation computation happens. Competency C-8.1 is the only row spanning all three measures.
Asks what a cumulative frequency table determines; the key is all three measures. LO-3 is the only outcome naming cumulative frequency, C-8.1 carries the all-three claim of the key.

Recovers a class limit from mid value and class width. Class-mark arithmetic is the setup step of the direct-mean method, the only outcome that uses class marks; there is no outcome for grouped-table structure itself.
Builds cumulative frequencies, locates N/2 and names the median class upper limit. Exactly the cumulative-frequency route of LO-3, not a mode or mean question.
Chooses the measure suited to the most frequent garment size, i.e. the mode. Conceptual rather than the modal-class formula, but LO-2 is the only mode outcome.
Manipulates Mode - Median = 2(Median - Mean) from the empirical relation. Spans all three measures with no single-measure calculation, so competency level, not LO-1/2/3.
Solves for x from a given mean, then means a second list. Pure direct-method mean arithmetic; median and mode are absent.
Tests that raising the top four of nine observations leaves the 5th (the median) fixed. Positional reasoning about the median, so LO-3.
The abscissa of the less-than/more-than ogive intersection is the median. This is the graphical route, which sits in C-8.2-LO-1, not the tabular cumulative-frequency route of C-8.1-LO-3.
Picks the most frequently occurring value of a raw list. Mode identification, LO-2; no grouped table, so no median-class or mean work.
Finds x from a given mean and then the mean of a sub-list. Direct-method mean only.
The key step is recognising that with a < b < c the median is b; the mean then supplies the sum. Median leads, mean is the secondary tool, so LO-3 before LO-1.
Orders seven algebraic observations and equates the 4th to the given median. Positional median work, LO-3, not a mode or mean calculation.
Two stages: the mean of squares fixes n = 17 (LO-1), then the median of the first 17 naturals is read off as the 9th term (LO-3). Both are load-bearing, mean first.
Applies the modal-class formula l + (f1-f0)/(2f1-f0-f2) * h to a grouped table. The textbook case of LO-2.
States the assumption behind the grouped mean: frequencies are taken as concentrated at class marks. That assumption belongs to the mean methods of LO-1, not to median or mode.
Substitutes into Mode = 3 Median - 2 Mean. The mode is the answer but no modal class exists, so LO-2 would misdescribe the work; competency level for the empirical relation.
The expenditure of the maximum number of workers is the mode; solved by the modal-class formula on the 1500-2000 class. LO-2, despite the mean-sounding word 'average' in the stem.
Converts a less-than table to ordinary frequencies only to find the largest one. The cumulative table is a means; the asked outcome is the modal class, so LO-2 not LO-3.
Derives Median:Mode from Mean:Median through the empirical relation. Three-measure relation with no single-measure computation, so competency level.
Modal-class formula applied to the traffic-count distribution. LO-2.
Uses Sum = 3M from the mean and the identity for (a+b+c)^2 to mean the squares. Direct-method mean reasoning throughout.
Identifies d_i in the assumed-mean formula as deviations of class marks. LO-1 fuses direct, assumed-mean and step-deviation, so there is no separate assumed-mean sibling to prefer.
